assumptions.summary: Oven temperature is constant and forced convection is present.
Pan conductivity is isotropic and high.
The pan is approximated as an open rectangular box.
Bottom heating is uniform and side facets drive edge nonuniformity.
Candidate polygons have equal area and share standard thermal parameters.
Polygons with sufficiently many edges may be treated as circles.
At most two pan shapes are used simultaneously on a rack.
The oven and pan environment is standard and R=1.

contributions.summary: Links heat conduction, convection, a Neumann boundary, and finite-element fields to edge-temperature dispersion.
Provides a compact inverse-square edge-count surrogate with a preserved intercept and fit limitations.
Combines unused area and normalized edge discrepancy through an explicit preference weight.
Restricts a practical integer vector to four shape families and at most two simultaneous shapes.
Turns close-packing diagrams into a center containment and counting procedure.
Pairs three parameter settings with selected layouts, dimensions, counts, and objective values.
Makes discrete recommendation boundaries visible to the stakeholder.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Standard lambda, h, T_ext, and q0 values enter the finite-element solve without calibration.
Nine edge-count cases provide variance, standard deviation, and normalized discrepancy values.
Commercial images and two 9 by 13 inch racks supply illustrative geometry.
Rack inches are converted to 754.8372 cm^2 and brownie area is fixed at 30 cm^2.

dependency_graph.closure_status: Positive interfaces are explicit, but dimensional closure, numerical convergence, fit diagnostics, and executable search details remain unresolved.
edges: Steady edge-temperature samples in kelvin are reduced to shape-specific edge standard deviations sigma_i.
Shape-specific sigma_i values and the rectangle baseline sigma_0 enter the normalized discrepancy objective.
Feasible counts N and dimensionless unused-area rate eta enter the weighted objective.
The retained shape family and candidate count vector determine which center lattice and containment test are evaluated.
Feasible arrangement count N returns to eta and the weighted objective for candidate comparison.
The R=1 objective, shape constraints, and discrepancy values define the worked test calculations.
Accepted center sets provide the visual layouts and feasible N values used in Tests 1-3.
Neighboring scenario selections and objective values expose discrete decision changes under p and W/L.
feedbacks: Center-matrix feasible N returns to eta and the objective before candidate selection.

independent_extensions.summary: Re-derive a dimensionally closed volumetric or boundary convection model with complete units.
Publish mesh, boundary implementation, tolerance, and spatial convergence evidence.
Fit sigma(m) with residuals, uncertainty, alternate forms, and held-out edge counts.
Elicit stakeholder utility or compute a Pareto frontier instead of asserting R and a linear scale.
Implement collision-aware mixed-shape packing with explicit lattice bounds, clearance, tie rules, and optimality gaps.
Map recommendation regions over p and W/L with uncertainty and decision-reversal boundaries.
Optimize rounded and irregular shapes and validate their thermal and packing performance before recommending them.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A six-paragraph requirement-method-result chain may improve answer retrieval; award coexistence is not causal evidence.
A visible flowchart may make geometric feasibility easier to audit; no judge source proves preference.
Pairing layouts with parameters and objective values may strengthen traceability; this is not proof of numerical validity.
A stakeholder artifact may make a design recommendation actionable, but its marketing claims must remain bounded by the model.

language_observations.summary: LP-A-ABS-FIND-DESIGN: Move from analysis to a diagnosed phenomenon and then to a design response.
LP-A-ABS-MODEL-ROLES: Inventory models and assign each a distinct responsibility.
LP-A-THEORY-METHOD-RESULT: Link physical principle, numerical method, observed output, and external consistency.
LP-A-EVIDENCE-DEFINE-FACTOR: Convert a requirement or prior result into a named decision factor.
LP-A-PURPOSE-NEXT-ACTION: State why the next analytical operation is necessary.
LP-A-DEFINE-FORMULA-WHERE: Introduce a mathematical definition and immediately resolve symbols and direction.
LP-A-INFERENCE-HANDOFF: Carry a computed or assumed result into the next modeling choice.
LP-A-FIGURE-TREND: Read a visible trend and translate it into an analytical implication.
LP-A-STAGE-GATE: Close the current subproblem and announce the next one.
LP-A-CONDITION-BRANCH: Route a weighted objective into interpretable limiting and mixed cases.
LP-A-CASE-GEOMETRY: State a geometry-specific feasibility rule before counting candidates.
LP-A-PROCEDURAL-SEQUENCE: Expose ordered operations and the output handed between them.
LP-A-INVARIANT-REPRESENTATION: Use a repeated structural invariant to justify an algorithmic representation.
LP-A-FORMAL-ADMISSIBILITY: State numbered or conjunctive admissibility conditions before accepting a candidate.
LP-A-TEST-SCENARIO-RESULT: Present a parameterized scenario, selected design, and objective value in one trace.
LP-A-CROSS-CASE-SYNTHESIS: Compare nearby cases while naming held and changed quantities.
LP-A-CONTRAST-CAVEAT: Pair a useful simplification or capability with its explicit limit.
LP-A-EVALUATION-MECHANISM: Evaluate each model by naming the mechanism behind a strength or limitation.
LP-A-IMPROVEMENT-ORDER: Convert a diagnosed limitation into a sequenced design extension.
LP-A-BOUNDARY-DISPOSITION: Separate technical evidence from bibliography, credits, and product-facing claims.

results_trace.summary: Edge-temperature standard deviation falls from 1.5139 for the square toward zero for the circle.
The fitted relation is sigma=23.605/m^2+0.035, with the source then using an inverse-square approximation.
p=0.5 and W/L=9/13 select 40 hexagons of edge 3.3981 cm at f=0.2956.
p=0.25 and W/L=9/13 select 30 octagons of edge 2.4926 cm at f=0.2546.
p=0.5 and W/L=0.6833 select 40 octagons at f=0.2050.
Small p or rack-ratio changes may cross an integer decision boundary.

Duplicate six-paragraph Summary content plus keywords; retained as occurrence aliases rather than new units.

Four assumptions, notation table, and open-top pan diagram.
Heat mechanisms, transient and steady PDEs, boundary condition, reduction, and finite elements.
Square/circle fields, polygon edge curves, Table 3, and Eq.6 fit.
Area and temperature factors, weighted objective, constraints, and three regimes.
Rectangle, circle, and mixed regular-polygon packing analyses.
Center lattice, boundary conditions, hexagon rotation, and flowchart.
Commercial rack geometry, arrangement catalogue, and three worked tests.
Discrete recommendation changes under p and W/L.
Separate positive mechanisms and limits for both models.
Rounded corners and nonregular polygon proposals ending on physical page 19.
Credits and four bibliography entries; provenance-only boundary.
Two product-facing pages; excluded from technical language and model evidence.

limitations: All 21 physical PDF pages were rendered and reviewed; printed numbering begins on physical PDF page 3.
Physical pages 1 and 2 duplicate the same six-paragraph Summary/Abstract route and are not double-counted as distinct language actions.
Physical pages 20-21 are advertising boundary material, not technical model evidence; the lower-left Circle Pans text on page 21 is visibly clipped.
The official 2013 Problem A statement is absent, so task reconstruction uses the paper's Summary and Introduction.

Construct and test feasible arrangements on a rectangular rack.

verification.summary: Curve-fit visualization without residual or holdout diagnostics.
Tests 2-3 arithmetic substitutions and neighboring-ratio comparison.
Local discrete p and W/L scenario comparison, not global robustness.

visualization_observations.summary: Open-top pan geometry defines bottom, sides, and boundary facets for the physical model.
Heat-flow arrows distinguish pan conduction and oven convection before the PDE.
Finite-element square temperature surface with kelvin colorbar shows corner concentration.
Square edge-temperature curve shows corner highs and edge-center lows against position.
Circle temperature surface supplies the near-uniform limiting comparison.
Aligned edge curves compare square through 16-gon under fixed area and parameters.
Numerical overall and edge dispersion statistics provide the optimization lookup.
Sigma versus inverse squared edge count visualizes the Eq.6 fit.
Packing sketches explain nominal area utilization and unused spaces.
Rack and rectangle dimensions expose the Eq.13 containment variables.
Rectangle arrangement illustrates the p=1 maximum-count branch.
Triangular and square circle-center lattices compare p=0 arrangements.
Rectangle, octagon, and hexagon diagrams show edge and interior waste mechanisms.
Dodecagon-to-circle comparison motivates the circle approximation for large m.
Heptagon and other polygon diagrams document excluded packing families.
Octagon edges and center matrix turn close packing into a point representation.
Hexagon diagram exposes the source's special boundary and rotation conditions.
Flowchart records input, matrix construction, containment tests, counting loop, and output.
Commercial oven, racks, and pan images establish scenario provenance but not validation data.
Two candidate arrangements for each retained shape define the search catalogue.
Test 1 hexagon layout visualizes N=40 for p=0.5 and W/L=9/13.
Test 2 octagon layout visualizes N=30 for p=0.25.
Test 3 octagon layout visualizes the neighboring aspect-ratio decision change.
Sharp-versus-rounded corner geometry and fields communicate a prospective improvement mechanism.

weaknesses.summary: The printed h unit makes Eq.3 and Eq.5 dimensionally incomplete unless an omitted interface factor or volumetric h is intended.
A first-normal-derivative boundary relation is called a third-order PDE.
The printed q0 unit W/(s m) is inconsistent with an ordinary heat-flux density.
The two-rack factor appears in Eq.7, Eq.12, Eq.15, and Eq.25 but disappears from Eq.11.
Variance, standard deviation, and per-unit values are not fully reconciled with sigma_i; tests use the per-unit standard-deviation values.
Compact grouping is clarified only when Eq.21 expands the objective.
W/L prose and Fig.9 L/W orientation are not reconciled.
The 4l-gon area relation lacks derivation and stable notation; transcription confidence is medium.
Z+ is undefined with respect to zero although absent-shape counts require zero.
The circumradius clearance exception is source-specific and not derived.
m>=12 and m>10 thresholds conflict, leaving m=11 unclassified.
Mesh, convergence, curve-fit diagnostics, search bounds, code, and tie rules are absent.
Rounded corners and nonregular polygons are prospective and not re-optimized or validated.
Taste, appetite, carbon, and user-category claims exceed the model; the Circle Pans paragraph is visibly clipped.

writing_logic.summary: Problem and finding -> model inventory -> physical evidence -> decision objective -> algorithm tests -> bounded evaluation.
Modeling intent -> three objectives -> four-stage work plan -> assumptions.
Environment -> material -> notation -> geometry -> physical model.
Grouped symbols -> definitions and units -> first governing equation.
Heat mechanisms -> dominant pathways -> design factors -> three preference regimes.
Transient law -> steady state -> boundary -> two-dimensional reduction -> finite-element output -> edge statistic.
Prior heat result -> utilization and discrepancy factors -> weighted objective -> limiting cases -> mixed shape vector.
Packing invariant -> center matrix -> boundary tests -> hexagon exception -> count output.
Commercial geometry -> candidate catalogue -> three parameterized tests -> objective values.
Mechanism plausibility -> fixed-area comparison -> arithmetic substitution -> neighboring-case decision check.
Integer vector -> discontinuity -> W/L and p comparisons -> decision-boundary caveat.
Model-by-model capability -> mechanism -> bounded positive use.
Model-by-model omission -> affected output -> safe scope.
Sharp-corner limit -> rounded design -> broader shape family -> prospective status.
